text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Alert - unusual outbound telemetry/beaconing detected from log-shipper-7 -> external IP range 13.59.0.0/16. Pattern matches known beacon signature 'TB-EXF-2026-02'. Count: 142 connections in last 5m.
oncall-maya: oncall here, paging sec-ops and infra. Maya: are we seeing customer-facing impact?
sec-ops: Sec here, looking. Initial indicator: repeated POSTs to /api/telemetry/v2 with compressed JSON blobs. Samples show keys with base64 blobs and user-agent "shipper/1.2.3".
infra-james: I can pull VPC flow logs and block egress to that /16 at edge if needed. Any false positives we should avoid?
sre-andy: service metrics: no increase in 5xxs, but some customer ingestion queues delayed ~30s for 3 customers in EU region. Correlating with same shippers.
oncall-maya: Block at edge for suspicious range, but only for shipper instances tagged 'staging' until we confirm. Put a rule that can be rolled back.
infra-james: rolling a security egress ACL denying 13.59.0.0/16 for tag:shipper-staging now. Command: `aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --cidr 13.59.0.0/16 --rule-action deny --protocol -1 --network-acl-id acl-xxxx`
sec-ops: grabbing a sample payload for forensics. Please preserve the last 12h log bucket (s3://redwood-shipper-raw/staging). Do not delete.
sre-andy: copying manifests for the 3 affected customers and pinning ingestion to a safe fallback endpoint. Adding a rate-limiter temporarily.
pagerbot: PagerDuty: Incident P12345 created and assigned to @oncall-maya.
sec-ops: sample payload (redacted):
```
{"hdr":"v2","payload":"eyJhY3QiOiJzaGlwIiwiZCI6Imh0dHA6Ly9leGZ1c2UuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vYmluIn0="}
```
sec-ops: suggests this looks like an exfil beacon that encodes pointers to blobs in our log archive. Could be automated exfil using compromised shipper credentials.
oncall-maya: sequencing: 1) containment, 2) assess customer blast radius, 3) key sweep/rotate if credentials confirmed, 4) legal/CS notif.
infra-james: containment done for staging shippers. I see 0 dropped connections since the ACL applied.
sec-ops: can someone snapshot the shipper instance(s) still running? Need disk image and process list.
sre-andy: creating snapshots now: `gcloud compute instances snapshot shipper-7 --snapshot-names shipper7-9490012345` (we have multi-cloud).
customer-success-olga: CS: reaching out to the 3 customers impacted to let them know we're investigating. No public disclosure yet.
legal-liaison: Legal: we need initial impact details and whether PII was present. If logs contain PII, follow breach-notification playbook.
sec-ops: pulling a quick grep of recent logs for keys/credentials referenced: `grep -E "api_key|auth_token|svcacct" /var/log/shipper/*.log | tail -n 200`
sec-ops: found two likely compromised tokens: svc-token-staging-abc123 and svc-token-staging-def456. They were used in outbound POSTs to 13.59.10.22 on 2026-03-12T02:14Z.
oncall-maya: rotate those two tokens now, and add a short-term deny-list for any tokens seen in outbound requests.
infra-james: rotating tokens via secrets manager: `redwood secrets rotate svc-token-staging-abc123` -> done for abc123, still rotating def456.
sec-ops: making a decision call: escalate to full key rotation for staging shipper role. Recommend: rotate all staging shipper tokens, revoke active sessions, forcibly restart shippers once new creds deployed.
sre-andy: we can roll deploy new token env var and restart in a controlled canary. ETA for rollout across staging fleet ~18m.
oncall-maya: approve full rotation for staging tokens, start canary. Maya: please capture timeline for postmortem.
pagerbot: Note: add tag `incident:P12345` to all related artifacts.
sec-ops: forensic note: exfil target domains include exfuse.example.com and 13.59.10.22. We're collecting DNS queries and outbound TLS certs.
customer-success-olga: CS update: customers A & B have reduced ingestion; C reports delayed historical logs. Offering status updates every 30m.
legal-liaison: Legal asks: preserve all S3 access logs and provide list of potentially exposed customer IDs.
infra-james: snapshot of s3 bucket performed: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-shipper-raw/staging s3://forensics/staging-snapshot --recursive --storage-class STANDARD_IA`
sec-ops: next steps: 1) finish token rotation (in progress), 2) confirm no active egress, 3) run full grep for PII markers in archived logs, 4) prepare initial incident summary for execs and legal.
oncall-maya: Maya handing off to @sec-ops for overnight monitoring and to coordinate legal/customer comms. If any customer escalation, page Maya directly.
sec-ops: taking over ops. Will file an internal timeline and slide deck for execs. Also opening a ticket to harden shipper auth (shorter TTLs, mutual TLS).
sre-andy: deployed canary with rotated tokens; no regressions. Rolling to rest of staging.
sec-ops: rotation complete for staging tokens. Recommend rotating prod shipper tokens next week as precaution, pending PM risk review.
legal-liaison: legal will prepare hold notice for affected customers and request data inventory.
customer-success-olga: CS will draft a personalized note to affected customers and await legal OK.
oncall-maya: closing initial bridge. Thanks everyone — tag any follow-ups with incident:P12345. :thumbsup:
sec-ops: logging final notes and keeping monitoring alert thresholds elevated for 72h.
